say.en: Pure nickel is made through a volatile carbonyl, the hardness of your tap water is measured with EDTA, and a platinum complex treats cancer. Coordination compounds are everywhere. In this lesson: Describe the structure and bonding of metal carbonyls.
List applications in analysis, metallurgy, biology and medicine.

body.en: Homoleptic carbonyls contain only CO ligands: Ni(CO)₄ (tetrahedral), Fe(CO)₅ (trigonal bipyramidal), Cr(CO)₆ (octahedral), Mn₂(CO)₁₀ (two square pyramids joined by a Mn–Mn bond) and Co₂(CO)₈ (a Co–Co bond bridged by two CO groups). The bonding is synergic: CO donates its carbon lone pair to an empty metal orbital (σ bond), and the metal donates a filled d pair back into the empty π* orbital of CO (π back-bond). Each strengthens the other, making the M–C bond strong while weakening C≡O.
body.kn: ಲೋಹ ಕಾರ್ಬೊನಿಲ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ CO ಕಾರ್ಬನ್‌ನ ಒಂಟಿ ಜೋಡಿಯನ್ನು ಲೋಹಕ್ಕೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ (σ ಬಂಧ), ಲೋಹ d ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳನ್ನು CO ಯ π* ಕಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಹಿಂದಿರುಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ (π ಹಿಂಬಂಧ). ಇದು ಸಹಕ್ರಿಯಾತ್ಮಕ ಬಂಧ.

The bonding is synergic: CO donates its carbon lone pair to an empty metal orbital sigma bond, and the metal donates a filled d pair back into the empty pi star orbital of CO (pi back-bond). Each strengthens the other, making the M-C bond strong while weakening C is equivalent to O.

title.en: On the board: metal carbonyls and uses

say.en: Metal carbonyls have CO bound to a metal in a low oxidation state. Some have metal–metal bonds.
CO gives a lone pair to the metal: sigma donation. The metal gives d electrons back into the empty pi star of CO: back bonding.
The two effects strengthen each other: the M–C bond gets stronger and the C–O bond weaker.
The EAN rule: many stable carbonyls reach the electron count of the next noble gas.
Complexes are everywhere: water hardness, nickel tests, cancer drugs, catalysts, metal extraction and the molecules of life.

problem.en: 50 mL of a water sample needs 10 mL of 0.01 M EDTA to complex all its Ca²⁺ (1 : 1). Express the hardness as ppm of CaCO₃.

steps.en: Moles of EDTA = 0.01 × 10/1000 = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol = moles of Ca²⁺ = moles of CaCO₃ equivalent.
Mass of CaCO₃ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ × 100 g mol⁻¹ = 0.01 g in 50 mL.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. 50 mL of a water sample needs 10 mL of 0.01 M EDTA to complex all its Ca²⁺ (1 : 1). Express the hardness as ppm of CaCO₃.

say.en: Let us solve this together. 50 millilitres of a water sample needs 10 millilitres of 0.01 M EDTA to complex all its Ca squared⁺ (1: 1). Express the hardness as ppm of CaCO 3.
Moles of EDTA equals 0.01 times 10 over 1000 equals 1.0 times 10 to the power minus 4 moles equals moles of Ca squared⁺ = moles of CaCO 3 equivalent.
Mass of CaCO 3 equals 1.0 times 10 to the power minus 4 times 100 grams mol to the power minus 1 equals 0.01 grams in 50 millilitres.
Per litre: 0.01 times 1000 over 50 equals 0.2 grams L to the power minus 1 equals 200 milligrams L to the power minus 1 equals 200 ppm.
So the answer is 200 ppm as CaCO 3.
